learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: Where does Euripides’ Medea begin?
Use the cited passage to explain: What distinguishes this play from the Argonautica?

main.work: The Tragedies of Euripides, Volume I
main.author: Euripides
main.locator: Medea, opening speech of the Nurse; local text, normalized characters 289402-289708
main.excerpt: and there marries Ægeus son of Pandion. * * * * * MEDEA. * * * * NURSE OF MEDEA. Would that the hull of Argo had not winged her way to the Colchian land through the Cyanean Symplegades,[1] and that the pine felled in the forests of Pelion had never fallen, nor had caused the hands of the chiefs to row,[2]
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Euripides starts in Corinth after the expedition. Jason has made a new marriage, and the Nurse fears what the abandoned Medea may do. This tragedy reshapes the heroic past into a crisis of oaths, exile, family, and revenge.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “and there marries Ægeus son of Pandion. * * * * * MEDEA. * * * * NURSE OF MEDEA. Would that the hull of Argo had not winged her way to the Colchian land through the Cyanean Symplegades,[1] and that the pine felled in the forests of Pelion had never fallen, nor had caused the hands of the chiefs to row,[2]”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: Tragedy changes the question from how the fleece was won to what Jason owed the woman whose knowledge made him succeed.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: The Nurse’s wish that the Argo had never sailed is a character’s speech in a tragedy. It reframes a remembered expedition; it is not a statement by Apollonius about how his own epic should be read.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the clearest lesson in why a myth is never fully described by naming the hero.

quiz.prompt: What distinguishes this play from the Argonautica?

choices.text: It stages a later crisis rather than narrating the quest itself.
It is a handbook arranging the twelve labours.
It is a victory ode for Jason’s chariot race.
